note: The lane priority contract (OMN-20074). classes lists the lane priority classes from highest to lowest; the last must be other, which a unit of no named class takes. A class at rank i leaves i free pool slots to the classes above it (handler_landing_placement.priority_holdback_refusal). repos names the repositories whose landing PRs are of a class; tickets names the parent tickets whose own work and children's work is of a class, and a ticket class outranks the repository class (an OCC retirement PR in an MVP repository is occ-retirement, not mvp-landing, because M4 work comes first). merge_ranks ranks open PRs for the landing controller, highest first, other last: a PR takes the first rank it meets. cause-fix is a declared cause fix (a cause lease's fix_ref, or fix= on an open cause CLAIM: a fix for a red base or a repository under its floor); process-fix is a PR in a repository, or of a ticket, listed under process-fix above; m4 is a PR whose title cites an M4 delegation carrier; pin-bump is a PR whose title matches a pin_bump_titles pattern (a pin or release bump that unblocks others); other is everything else. The controller dispatches workers and enqueues in rank order, and while a merge-queue base is red and a cause-fix PR is open on it, it enqueues nothing else there and dequeues the other entries (landing_controller.red_base_gates). landing_placement.load_priority_contract reads this file (ONEX_LANE_PRIORITY_CLASSES overrides the path); pool_reading_max_age_s (OMN-21809, orchestrator decision 2026-10-31 on the pool-status timeout) is how many seconds a host's last good probe reading may stand in for a live read that timed out under concurrent readers: landing_placement.read_pool uses it, marks the Reading cached and says so in the receipt, and past it the host reads UNREADABLE; the probe timeout is not raised. Reordering a class or a rank is an edit here and a new ruling, never a list in code.
